where: Section 1, formula line T_p = Θ(log n), W = p · T_p = Θ(n)
problem: The equality W = p · T_p is false here. The line itself sets p = n, so p · T_p = n · Θ(log n) = Θ(n log n), not Θ(n). The two claims contradict each other, and a student who copies W = p·T_p into an answer loses marks.
fix: Total work is Θ(n) because the round sizes n, 3n/4, 9n/16, ... sum to 4n, not because processors × time multiplies out. Write: T_p = Θ(log n) when p = n; W = Θ(n) total work over all rounds. Note that p · T_p = Θ(n log n) is only the processor-time product and counts processors that sit idle in later rounds, so it is not the work.

problem: The binary-search steps are wrong. After a[7] = 34 < 42 the low end must move, not the high end, and one comparison is skipped: the text jumps from mid = 7 to mid = 9, which is impossible when lo = 8 and hi = 14 (that midpoint is 11). Only two comparisons are described while the answer claims three.
fix: mid = 7, a[7] = 34 < 42, so lo = 8. mid = 11, a[11] = 51 > 42, so hi = 10. mid = 9, a[9] = 42; found at index 9 in 3 comparisons.

where: Section 1, list of steps after the prefix sum
problem: Only the branch k > r is given (and its condition is garbled as 'If k  r'). The branch k < r is missing, so the stated algorithm never says what to do when the answer lies below the pivot, even though the worked example needs exactly that branch.
fix: If r = k, return the pivot. If k < r, keep the keys below the pivot, leave k unchanged, and repeat on the survivors. If k > r, keep the keys above the pivot, replace k by k − r, and repeat on the survivors.

where: Section 1, paragraph 'The pivot is never extreme'
problem: The counting is loose for even block sizes. With the median taken at position ⌈m/2⌉ (the lower median) and m even, only m/2 − 1 keys lie strictly below the block median, and only ⌈p/2⌉ − 1 block medians lie strictly below the pivot. The conclusion n/4 survives only if you count 'at or below'.
fix: At least ⌈p/2⌉ block medians are ≤ the pivot, and each of those blocks has at least ⌈m/2⌉ keys ≤ its own median, so at least (p/2)(m/2) = n/4 keys are ≤ the pivot; the same argument gives at least n/4 keys ≥ the pivot.

problem: The prefix sum of the p counts gives the number of keys strictly below the pivot, which is r − 1, not r. The text says it 'gives the pivot's true rank r'.
fix: The prefix sum of the p counts gives the number of keys below the pivot; the pivot's rank is r = that count + 1.

problem: The edge labels do not match their notes and do not describe the ranges correctly: an edge labelled '≤ 34' carries the note '17 to 34', and an edge labelled '≤ 17' carries 'below 17' although 17 itself is inside it. A student reading the tree gets contradictory ranges.
fix: Label the four edges 'x ≤ 17', '17 < x ≤ 34', '34 < x ≤ 51', 'x > 51', and drop the 'below 17' / '17 to 34' notes.

problem: The bullet points the wrong way. Reading the p per-block answers in one step is cheap on a PRAM, so the block-split time really is Θ(log(n/p)); the full answer including the combine step is Θ(log(n/p) + log p) = Θ(log n), not something smaller. As written, the trap suggests that adding the combine step makes the time longer than O(log n), which is the opposite of what happens.
fix: Say: dropping the combine step leaves the p per-block answers unread, so no answer is reported; the combine costs O(1) with a concurrent read or O(log p) as a reduction, giving Θ(log(n/p) + log p) = Θ(log n) in total. Reporting only O(log(n/p)) is right only when the combine is counted as O(1).
